# Independent audit: fixed-facet contraction and a tied endpoint

Source: `candidate 0e094dd9f76aefdd`.

**Result: PASS, every section.** The source verifier passes 1,291 exact
checks. No repair identified. The support/section sufficient inequalities
remain explicit assumptions; no automatic balance is inferred.

## 1. C1 section data and the actual equal-budget path

For a planar convex body, its section-length function in a fixed normal
direction is finite and concave on the open support interval, hence
continuous there. Proper positive-area cuts have thresholds strictly
inside that interval. Fubini with the scalar normal coordinate gives
the cap-area derivative as minus H_1(section)/||v_i||. The stated sigma
factors therefore have the exact coarea normalization for nonunit normals.

The pulled-back homothety threshold (b-t*v_i.p)/(1-t) and multiplier
(1-t)^2 show joint C1 dependence on the source and t. This formula also
extends to a small negative-t neighborhood for the implicit-function
argument; compatibility is used only for the authorized positive-t
contraction. No second derivatives or smooth boundary are assumed.

The B trace remains exactly its supporting face for every moving source;
it has zero area. The A threshold is 2v_i.y-h_i and the K threshold v_i.y,
so the source gradient is -(2sigma_Ai+sigma_Ki)v_i. The three unknowns
(y,q) have nonsingular derivative: multiplication by lambda_i=1/s_i
and summation first forces delta_q=0, then spanning forces delta_y=0.
The C1 implicit-function theorem supplies the path, which stays interior
to K and in the proper-section neighborhood. Every cap remains an actual
ambient cap through that common source.

## 2. All-source upper certificate and support optimum

The three middle traces cover the entire plane because their normals
sum to zero. Thus their common mass bounds the depth of EVERY middle
point, whether or not the displayed normals are minimizing after the
variation. The integer endpoints admit finite isolation of arbitrary
ordinary caps, and their fiber maxima therefore equal the ordinary
maxima. Nested contractions preserve midpoint compatibility and the
three induced fibers exactly. This proves the maximum-of-three upper
certificate without any normal-gap or criticality-persistence assumption.

Differentiating the exact homothety formula gives the loss
L_i(p)=2U_i+(b_i-v_i.p)sigma_Ai. The moving source term is -s_i v_i.y',
which cancels after multiplication by lambda_i and summation. The common
budget derivative is therefore -Lbar. Since each contracted cap is nested
inside its original cap, every L_i(p)>=0, including boundary choices of p.

Lbar is affine in p on compact A. Maximizing its negative linear part
produces precisely h_A(-sum lambda_i sigma_Ai v_i), with the sign stated
in (5), and the maximum is attained. No incompatible choices of several
contraction centers are combined in this formula.

## 3. Normalized descent and shell balance

Under original global depth Q and strict endpoint gaps, the certificate
q(t) remains above the two endpoint maxima near zero. Since M'(0)=-2a,
the derivative of q(t)/M(t) has numerator -M*Lbar+2aQ. The strict descent
criterion follows, and Lbar>=4a/9 is sufficient under the STRICT bad
premise Q/M<2/9. Equality with the target is not silently included.

The three fixed A caps cover the plane: sum b_i=-sum h_B(v_i)<0, with
strictness obtained at any interior point of B. Their removed cap masses
are the actual intersections of A minus A_t with these fixed caps.
Coverage yields sum L_i>=2a after differentiating the shell identity.
Together with nonnegativity this gives Lbar>=2a lambda_min/Lambda.
The ratio condition max s/min s<=7/4 implies the claimed fraction at
least 2/9 by Lambda/lambda_min<=1+2*(7/4). All constants check.

For the support-sensitive improvement, choose ONE actual p maximizing
L_j. Write sum lambda_i L_i=lambda_min sum L_i plus nonnegative excess
terms, retain only the j term, and use the attained support formula for
L_j. This proves (14). Taking the best index does not require a single
point to maximize several different losses simultaneously.

## 4. Missing-corner shell load

At any A point, at least one fixed cap is captured. A unique captured
cap i puts that point exactly in the strict residual region R_i; hence
an absent R_i excludes that singleton incidence. All remaining possible
incidences have weight at least the stated tau, and triple weight exceeds
any pair weight. The same pointwise inequality holds on every removed
shell. Integration followed by the proved C1 differentiation gives
sum lambda_i L_i>=2a tau.

The second-smallest-weight and two-smallest-weight consequences follow
directly from this finite incidence list. If a residual is merely
area-null, it contributes zero to every shell and the same integrated
inequality holds; strict emptiness requires no null-set qualification.
No freely chosen or averaged profile replaces the actual A geometry.

## 5. Tied-B two-rate criterion

With rates u,v and centers p,q, both endpoint homotheties are nested and
maintain actual compatibility. The moving support is exactly
h_i-vt(h_i-v_i.q). The A threshold therefore moves upward by
v(h_i-v_i.q) in addition to its source movement and own contraction.
Its extra derivative is -v*sigma_Ai(h_i-v_i.q). B's captured area remains
identically zero at its own moving support; there is no omitted B-area
term. Summing the equal-budget equations gives -uLbar-vJbar as claimed.
The B support optimum has the same negative sign in h_B(-V), and Jbar
is nonnegative at every actual q in B.

The normalized menu derivative is negative exactly under the first
strict inequality (19). The tied endpoint derivative is negative exactly
under Qv>r(au+bv). The formerly strict A gap remains harmless. Thus both
upper bounds decrease strictly together under the displayed two tests.
For u>0 the endpoint test is t_ratio>a/(a+k). If J<=2rb, the first test
has nonpositive slope in t_ratio, so a feasible strictly admissible ratio
exists iff its boundary value is positive, equivalently
(a+k)L+aJ>2aQ. The zero-slope case has the same strict requirement.
For J>2rb, a sufficiently large ratio works, and B-only contraction also
works. These are precisely first-order certificate tests, not necessary
conditions for all possible geometric deformations.

Because the two centers lie independently in A and B and the two rates
are nonnegative, their separately attained support maxima can be used
simultaneously. No tied endpoint is silently discarded, and no missing
corner or small-volume premise is asserted to force these thresholds.
